of art, or when our experience convinces us of divine gracious-
ness, or when we are shattered by a momentous historical
event in which we feel compelled to see a manifestation of
divine judgment. And we are right at such times to feel
deeply aware of the wonder-working action of the Creator
of all things. But we must admit at the same time that there
are other men who see and experience the same things but
who view and interpret them quite differently; who are
unable to detect in them evidence of God's rule, or to hear in
them God's voice.
This situation calls our attention to the most important
point of all, namely that the creative action of God is not
something which lies unbared to the eyes of all so that all
must see and recognize it. No, God's creative action can
only be apprehended when I experience something of it in my
own life. Belief in God the Creator of heaven and earth is not
a theoretical truth the rightness of which may be realized on
the ground of demonstrative reasons, and of which a man
might persuade himself once for all so as to be able to say:
"If God is the Creator of the world, then He is also my
Creator; if He is the Author of all that is, then He is also
the Author of my own destiny." Belief of this kind often
collapses sharply when a man is struck down by a dark and
tragic fate. If he is no longer convinced that God is his
Creator, he also ceases to be convinced that God must be
the Creator of the world.
The truth in fact is that I can only believe in God as the
Creator of the world, when I see that truth reflected in my
own life and experience. When Luther in the Shorter Catech-
ism explains the first article of belief: "I believe in God the
Father almighty, Creator of heaven and earth"
, he says:
"What does this mean?" Answer: "I believe that God has
created me together with all other creatures." The "I believe
that God has created me" is the primary matter. Only when
I have reached certitude on that point, can I also believe
that God has created all creatures. And for the same reason
